title: CTS Radical Christianity — Unit 7: Be Humble

blocks.en: 📖 Radical Christianity: The Ten Commandments of Jesus — Unit 7: Be Humble
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Cristianismo Radical: Los Diez Mandamientos de Jesús — Unidad 7: Sed Humildes

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "...be clothed with humility, for 'God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.'" — 1 Peter 5:5 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "...revestíos de humildad; porque: Dios resiste a los soberbios, y da gracia a los humildes." — 1 Pedro 5:5 (RVG)

blocks.en: 1. The Divine Economy: Down Is the Way Up
blocks.es_reference: 1. La Economía Divina: Abajo Es el Camino Hacia Arriba

blocks.en: 1 Peter 5:5-6 (NKJV): "Yes, all of you be submissive to one another, and be clothed with humility, for 'God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.' Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time."
blocks.es_reference: 1 Pedro 5:5-6 (RVG): "Y todos, sumisos unos a otros, revestíos de humildad; porque: Dios resiste a los soberbios, y da gracia a los humildes. Humillaos, pues, bajo la poderosa mano de Dios, para que él os exalte cuando fuere tiempo."

blocks.en: This command runs directly against the grain of everything the world teaches us about getting ahead. We are told to assert ourselves, promote ourselves, and climb; Jesus tells us to humble ourselves. And Peter gives the reason in one startling sentence: God actively resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble. Pride does not merely displease God; it sets a person against the current of His grace, while humility opens the heart to receive it.
blocks.es_reference: Este mandamiento va directamente contra la corriente de todo lo que el mundo nos enseña sobre prosperar. Se nos dice que nos afirmemos, nos promovamos y escalemos; Jesús nos dice que nos humillemos. Y Pedro da la razón en una frase asombrosa: Dios resiste activamente a los soberbios, pero da gracia a los humildes. La soberbia no solo desagrada a Dios; pone a la persona contra la corriente de su gracia, mientras que la humildad abre el corazón para recibirla.

blocks.en: So the whole of the Christian life runs on an inverted economy: the way up is down. "Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God," Peter says, "that He may exalt you in due time." We do not climb to greatness; we lower ourselves, and trust God to lift us in His own time and way. This is not a strategy for getting exalted — that would just be pride wearing humility's clothes — but a genuine surrender that leaves the lifting to God.
blocks.es_reference: Así que toda la vida cristiana corre sobre una economía invertida: el camino hacia arriba es hacia abajo. "Humillaos bajo la poderosa mano de Dios," dice Pedro, "para que él os exalte cuando fuere tiempo." No escalamos hacia la grandeza; nos abajamos, y confiamos en que Dios nos levante a su tiempo y a su manera. Esto no es una estrategia para ser exaltados — eso solo sería soberbia vestida de humildad — sino una entrega genuina que deja el levantar en manos de Dios.

blocks.en: 2. What Humility Is — and Is Not
blocks.es_reference: 2. Lo Que la Humildad Es — y No Es

blocks.en: We must be careful here, because humility is easily misunderstood as self-hatred, groveling, or a low opinion of ourselves. That is not what Scripture means. Humility is not thinking poorly of yourself; it is, as it has well been said, that true servants do not think less of themselves — they simply think of themselves less. The proud person and the self-loathing person are actually alike in one way: both are absorbed with themselves. Humility is the freedom of a self that has stopped staring at itself at all.
blocks.es_reference: Debemos tener cuidado aquí, porque la humildad se malentiende fácilmente como odio a uno mismo, servilismo, o una baja opinión de nosotros mismos. No es eso lo que la Escritura quiere decir. La humildad no es pensar mal de ti mismo; es, como bien se ha dicho, que los verdaderos siervos no piensan menos de sí mismos — sencillamente piensan menos en sí mismos. El soberbio y el que se desprecia a sí mismo en realidad se parecen en una cosa: ambos están absortos en sí mismos. La humildad es la libertad de un yo que ha dejado de mirarse a sí mismo del todo.

blocks.en: Paul gives the positive shape of it: "let nothing be done through selfish ambition or conceit, but in lowliness of mind let each esteem others better than himself" (Philippians 2:3). Humility looks outward and upward — reckoning others as worth genuine attention and care, and God as worthy of all. It does not require pretending we have no gifts; it requires remembering that whatever we have is a gift, received, not achieved. The humble person can receive a compliment or a correction with the same steadiness, because his sense of worth no longer rests on either.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo da su forma positiva: "nada hagáis por contienda o por vanagloria; antes bien con humildad, estimándoos inferiores los unos a los otros" (Filipenses 2:3). La humildad mira hacia afuera y hacia arriba — considerando a los demás dignos de verdadera atención y cuidado, y a Dios digno de todo. No exige fingir que no tenemos dones; exige recordar que todo lo que tenemos es un don, recibido, no logrado. El humilde puede recibir un elogio o una corrección con la misma serenidad, porque su sentido de valor ya no descansa en ninguno de los dos.

blocks.en: 3. Pride: The Root Sin
blocks.es_reference: 3. La Soberbia: El Pecado Raíz

blocks.en: To see why humility matters so much, we have to see what it cures. Pride is not just one sin among many; it is closer to the root of them all. "Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall" (Proverbs 16:18). It was pride that first turned a creature against the Creator, the desire to be as God, to sit at the center where only God belongs. Every other sin has some of that same self-exaltation tangled into it.
blocks.es_reference: Para ver por qué importa tanto la humildad, hay que ver qué cura. La soberbia no es solo un pecado entre muchos; está más cerca de ser la raíz de todos. "Antes del quebrantamiento es la soberbia; y antes de la caída la altivez de espíritu" (Proverbios 16:18). Fue la soberbia lo que primero volvió a una criatura contra el Creador, el deseo de ser como Dios, de sentarse en el centro donde solo Dios pertenece. Todo otro pecado tiene algo de esa misma autoexaltación enredada en él.

blocks.en: This is why God must resist the proud: pride is the human heart usurping God's throne, and His opposition to it is mercy, not cruelty. Charles Colson named the modern forms of it plainly — we must repent of idolatry, of having embraced the false gods of our time: materialism, power, success, and personal autonomy. Each of these is a way of making ourselves the center. Humility is simply the truth coming back into focus: God is God, and we are His creatures, dependent on Him for every breath. Far from being demeaning, that truth is the only solid ground a soul can stand on.
blocks.es_reference: Por esto Dios debe resistir a los soberbios: la soberbia es el corazón humano usurpando el trono de Dios, y su oposición a ella es misericordia, no crueldad. Charles Colson nombró sus formas modernas con claridad — debemos arrepentirnos de la idolatría, de haber abrazado los falsos dioses de nuestro tiempo: el materialismo, el poder, el éxito, y la autonomía personal. Cada uno de estos es una manera de hacernos a nosotros mismos el centro. La humildad es sencillamente la verdad volviendo a enfocarse: Dios es Dios, y nosotros somos sus criaturas, dependientes de Él por cada aliento. Lejos de ser degradante, esa verdad es el único suelo firme sobre el cual un alma puede pararse.

blocks.en: 4. The Mind of Christ
blocks.es_reference: 4. La Mente de Cristo

blocks.en: Philippians 2:5-8 (NKJV): "Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus, who, being in the form of God... made Himself of no reputation, taking the form of a bondservant, and coming in the likeness of men. And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to the point of death, even the death of the cross."
blocks.es_reference: Filipenses 2:5-8 (RVG): "Haya, pues, en vosotros este sentir que hubo también en Cristo Jesús; el cual, siendo en forma de Dios... se anonadó a sí mismo, tomando forma de siervo, hecho semejante a los hombres; y hallado en la condición de hombre, se humilló a sí mismo, haciéndose obediente hasta la muerte, y muerte de cruz."

blocks.en: The deepest reason to be humble is that humility is the very mind of Christ. He who was God in His own right did not cling to His rights. He made Himself of no reputation, took the form of a servant, and humbled Himself all the way down to the death of the cross. The whole movement of His life was downward — from heaven's throne to a manger, from glory to a cross — and every step of that descent was service.
blocks.es_reference: La razón más honda para ser humildes es que la humildad es la mismísima mente de Cristo. Él, que era Dios por derecho propio, no se aferró a sus derechos. Se anonadó a sí mismo, tomó forma de siervo, y se humilló todo el camino hasta la muerte de cruz. Todo el movimiento de su vida fue hacia abajo — del trono del cielo a un pesebre, de la gloria a una cruz — y cada paso de ese descenso fue servicio.

blocks.en: This means humility is not finally a technique or a personality trait; it is Christlikeness. When we lower ourselves to serve, when we esteem others, when we refuse to grasp at our rights, we are thinking the very thoughts of Jesus and walking the path He walked. The call to be humble is the call to "let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus" — to let His downward, self-giving love become the pattern of our own.
blocks.es_reference: Esto significa que la humildad no es al final una técnica ni un rasgo de personalidad; es la semejanza a Cristo. Cuando nos abajamos para servir, cuando estimamos a los demás, cuando rehusamos aferrarnos a nuestros derechos, estamos pensando los mismísimos pensamientos de Jesús y caminando el sendero que Él caminó. El llamado a ser humildes es el llamado a tener "este sentir que hubo también en Cristo Jesús" — a dejar que su amor descendente y abnegado se vuelva el patrón del nuestro.

blocks.en: 5. The World's Ladder Inverted
blocks.es_reference: 5. La Escalera del Mundo Invertida

blocks.en: Once we see the mind of Christ, we realize how completely it overturns the world's whole scale of values. As Colson put it, every standard the world uses to judge men is the opposite of God's measure. The world says: to be rich is to be blessed — but in God's economy the poor in spirit are blessed. The world says: to be recognized and applauded is to have arrived — but God exalts the humble. The world says: to be powerful is to be great — but Jesus says you must become a servant to be great.
blocks.es_reference: Una vez que vemos la mente de Cristo, nos damos cuenta de cuán completamente trastorna toda la escala de valores del mundo. Como dijo Colson, todo criterio que el mundo usa para juzgar a los hombres es lo opuesto de la medida de Dios. El mundo dice: ser rico es ser bendecido — pero en la economía de Dios los pobres en espíritu son bendecidos. El mundo dice: ser reconocido y aplaudido es haber llegado — pero Dios exalta al humilde. El mundo dice: ser poderoso es ser grande — pero Jesús dice que debes hacerte siervo para ser grande.

blocks.en: This is not a minor adjustment to the world's ladder; it is a different ladder entirely, pointing the other direction. The kingdom of God does not run on the same fuel as the kingdoms of men. And this is liberating news, because it means the whole exhausting race for status and recognition is one we are free to step out of. We no longer have to claw our way up, because in Christ the lowest place has become the place of honor, and the towel has become greater than the crown.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es un ajuste menor a la escalera del mundo; es una escalera enteramente distinta, que apunta en la otra dirección. El reino de Dios no funciona con el mismo combustible que los reinos de los hombres. Y ésta es noticia liberadora, porque significa que toda la agotadora carrera por el estatus y el reconocimiento es una de la que somos libres para salir. Ya no tenemos que abrirnos paso a las uñas hacia arriba, porque en Cristo el lugar más bajo se ha vuelto el lugar de honor, y la toalla se ha vuelto más grande que la corona.

blocks.en: 6. Greatness Is Servanthood
blocks.es_reference: 6. La Grandeza Es Servir

blocks.en: Matthew 20:25-28 (NKJV): "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them... Yet it shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you, let him be your servant... just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many."
blocks.es_reference: Mateo 20:25-28 (RVG): "Sabéis que los príncipes de los gentiles se enseñorean sobre ellos... Mas entre vosotros no será así; sino que el que quisiere ser grande entre vosotros, será vuestro servidor... así como el Hijo del Hombre no vino para ser servido, sino para servir, y para dar su vida en rescate por muchos."

blocks.en: Jesus did not abolish the desire for greatness; He redirected it. He says plainly, "it shall not be so among you." Among the nations, greatness means having others under you; in the kingdom, greatness means getting under others to lift them. Whoever would be great must be a servant. And He proves it not merely by teaching but by example: the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús no abolió el deseo de grandeza; lo redirigió. Dice con claridad: "entre vosotros no será así." Entre las naciones, la grandeza significa tener a otros bajo uno; en el reino, la grandeza significa ponerse debajo de otros para levantarlos. El que quiera ser grande debe ser siervo. Y lo prueba no solo enseñando sino con el ejemplo: el Hijo del Hombre no vino para ser servido sino para servir, y para dar su vida en rescate por muchos.

blocks.en: On the night He was betrayed, knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, Jesus rose from supper, wrapped a towel around His waist, and washed His disciples' feet — including the feet of Judas, who would betray Him within hours. The Lord of glory took the slave's task, and then said, "you also ought to wash one another's feet." Here is the whole lesson in a single picture: real greatness kneels. Jesus also warned of the opposite spirit — the love of titles and the chief seats — and said simply, "whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted" (Matthew 23:12).
blocks.es_reference: La noche en que fue entregado, sabiendo que el Padre había puesto todas las cosas en sus manos, Jesús se levantó de la cena, se ciñó una toalla a la cintura, y lavó los pies de sus discípulos — incluidos los pies de Judas, que lo traicionaría en pocas horas. El Señor de la gloria tomó la tarea del esclavo, y luego dijo: "vosotros también debéis lavaros los pies los unos a los otros." Aquí está toda la lección en una sola imagen: la verdadera grandeza se arrodilla. Jesús también advirtió del espíritu opuesto — el amor a los títulos y a los primeros asientos — y dijo sencillamente: "el que se enaltece será humillado, y el que se humilla será enaltecido" (Mateo 23:12).

blocks.en: The towel and the nail: I once attended a service where the pastor reenacted the closing days of Jesus' life. Everyone was asked to remove their shoes, and each person knelt and washed another's feet — humility is something you do, not merely admire. Then, at the front, stood a wooden cross with a nail set in it, and every one of us took a turn driving that nail in, to confess that we had all helped nail Jesus to the cross. The deepest humility is not merely thinking ourselves lower than other people; it is knowing we are sinners for whom Christ had to die — that our own pride helped drive the nail.
blocks.es_reference: La toalla y el clavo: Una vez asistí a un culto donde el pastor representó los últimos días de la vida de Jesús. Se pidió a todos que se quitaran los zapatos, y cada persona se arrodilló y lavó los pies de otra — la humildad es algo que se hace, no solo que se admira. Luego, al frente, había una cruz de madera con un clavo puesto en ella, y cada uno de nosotros tomó su turno para clavar ese clavo, confesando que todos habíamos ayudado a clavar a Jesús en la cruz. La humildad más honda no es solo pensarnos más bajos que las demás personas; es saber que somos pecadores por quienes Cristo tuvo que morir — que nuestra propia soberbia ayudó a clavar el clavo.

blocks.en: 7. Humility Among God's People
blocks.es_reference: 7. La Humildad Entre el Pueblo de Dios

blocks.en: This has sharp implications for how the church itself is meant to function. Too often we have borrowed our patterns of leadership from the empire, the military, and the corporate world, building religious hierarchies where men rule over men — the very thing Jesus said should not be so among us. Pride dressed in religious clothing produces domination, manipulation, and the autocratic rule of the few over the many, and it ends in personal failure. The early church knew a different way: leaders who walked in humility, submitted to one another, served rather than dominated, and released others into ministry rather than using them.
blocks.es_reference: Esto tiene implicaciones agudas para cómo la iglesia misma ha de funcionar. Con demasiada frecuencia hemos tomado prestados nuestros patrones de liderazgo del imperio, lo militar, y el mundo corporativo, construyendo jerarquías religiosas donde los hombres se enseñorean de los hombres — justo lo que Jesús dijo que no debía ser así entre nosotros. La soberbia vestida de ropa religiosa produce dominación, manipulación, y el gobierno autocrático de unos pocos sobre los muchos, y termina en fracaso personal. La iglesia primitiva conocía otra manera: líderes que andaban en humildad, sumisos unos a otros, que servían en vez de dominar, y que soltaban a otros al ministerio en vez de usarlos.

blocks.en: Humility also shows up in something quieter: the willingness to be honest about our own struggles. Paul says, "bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ" (Galatians 6:2). It takes humility to admit we have burdens at all — to stop pretending we have it all together and to let fellow believers actually help us. A proud heart hides its troubles to protect its image; a humble heart is vulnerable and forthright about what is really going on, and so receives the very grace and support God intends to give through others.
blocks.es_reference: La humildad también se muestra en algo más callado: la disposición a ser honestos sobre nuestras propias luchas. Pablo dice: "sobrellevad los unos las cargas de los otros, y cumplid así la ley de Cristo" (Gálatas 6:2). Hace falta humildad para admitir que tenemos cargas en absoluto — para dejar de fingir que lo tenemos todo bajo control y dejar que otros creyentes de veras nos ayuden. Un corazón soberbio esconde sus problemas para proteger su imagen; un corazón humilde es vulnerable y franco sobre lo que de veras está pasando, y así recibe la misma gracia y apoyo que Dios quiere dar por medio de otros.

blocks.en: 8. He Will Exalt You in Due Time
blocks.es_reference: 8. Él Te Exaltará a Su Tiempo

blocks.en: Luke 18:13-14 (NKJV): "And the tax collector, standing afar off, would not so much as raise his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me a sinner!' I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted."
blocks.es_reference: Lucas 18:13-14 (RVG): "Mas el publicano, estando lejos, no quería ni aun alzar los ojos al cielo, sino que hería su pecho, diciendo: Dios, sé propicio a mí, pecador. Os digo que éste descendió a su casa justificado antes que el otro; porque cualquiera que se enaltece, será humillado; y el que se humilla, será enaltecido."

blocks.en: Jesus pictured two men praying: a proud Pharisee, who informed God of his virtues, and a tax collector, who could only beg for mercy. It was the broken, humble man — not the impressive one — who went home justified. This is the divine economy at work: God resists the one and gives grace to the other. The way up really is down.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús pintó a dos hombres orando: un fariseo soberbio, que informaba a Dios de sus virtudes, y un publicano, que solo podía rogar misericordia. Fue el hombre quebrantado y humilde — no el impresionante — quien descendió a su casa justificado. Ésta es la economía divina en acción: Dios resiste al uno y da gracia al otro. El camino hacia arriba de veras es hacia abajo.

blocks.en: And there is a promise folded into the command. "Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time." We are not asked to grovel in the dust forever; we are asked to take the low place and trust God to do the lifting, in His time, in His way. The pattern is Christ's own: He humbled Himself to the death of the cross, and therefore God highly exalted Him and gave Him the name above every name. The descent was real, and so was the exaltation that followed. What we surrender to God's mighty hand, that hand will one day raise.
blocks.es_reference: Y hay una promesa plegada dentro del mandamiento. "Humillaos bajo la poderosa mano de Dios, para que él os exalte cuando fuere tiempo." No se nos pide que nos arrastremos en el polvo para siempre; se nos pide que tomemos el lugar bajo y confiemos en que Dios haga el levantar, a su tiempo, a su manera. El patrón es el de Cristo mismo: se humilló hasta la muerte de cruz, y por eso Dios le exaltó hasta lo sumo y le dio un nombre que es sobre todo nombre. El descenso fue real, y también lo fue la exaltación que siguió. Lo que entregamos a la poderosa mano de Dios, esa mano un día lo levantará.

blocks.en: 9. Clothe Yourselves With Humility
blocks.es_reference: 9. Revestíos de Humildad

blocks.en: So Peter's command comes back to us with all its weight and all its hope: "be clothed with humility." It is a garment we put on deliberately, the way Jesus deliberately wrapped Himself in a towel. We do not wait to feel humble; we choose to think of ourselves less, to esteem others, to take the lower place, to serve. And as we do, we discover we are not diminished but freed — freed from the exhausting work of defending and promoting ourselves, freed to love.
blocks.es_reference: Así que el mandamiento de Pedro nos vuelve con todo su peso y toda su esperanza: "revestíos de humildad." Es una prenda que nos ponemos deliberadamente, como Jesús deliberadamente se ciñó una toalla. No esperamos a sentirnos humildes; elegimos pensar menos en nosotros mismos, estimar a los demás, tomar el lugar más bajo, servir. Y al hacerlo, descubrimos que no somos disminuidos sino librados — librados del agotador trabajo de defendernos y promovernos, librados para amar.

blocks.en: Humility, then, is not one more item on a list of virtues to achieve. It is the shape of a life that has caught the mind of Christ — the God who left His throne, took a towel, and knelt. To be humble is to follow Him down, in the confidence that the God who raised Him will, in due time, raise all who walk that downward road with Him. God resists the proud, but to the humble He gives grace upon grace.
blocks.es_reference: La humildad, entonces, no es un elemento más en una lista de virtudes que alcanzar. Es la forma de una vida que ha captado la mente de Cristo — el Dios que dejó su trono, tomó una toalla, y se arrodilló. Ser humilde es seguirlo hacia abajo, con la confianza de que el Dios que lo levantó, a su tiempo, levantará a todos los que caminen ese camino descendente con Él. Dios resiste a los soberbios, pero al humilde le da gracia sobre gracia.

mc.stem: According to 1 Peter 5:5, how does God respond to the proud and to the humble?
options: He resists the proud but gives grace to the humble
mc.why: God actively resists the proud but gives grace to the humble; pride sets a person against grace, while humility opens the heart to receive it.

mc.stem: What is the 'inverted economy' of the Christian life described in the lesson?
options: The way up is down — we humble ourselves and let God exalt us
mc.why: The way up is down: we humble ourselves under God's mighty hand and trust Him to exalt us in due time, rather than climbing by self-promotion.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what is humility NOT?
options: Self-hatred or a low opinion of oneself
mc.why: Humility is not self-hatred or a low opinion of oneself; the proud and the self-loathing are alike absorbed with self.

mc.stem: The lesson sums up humility with which memorable line?
options: True servants don't think less of themselves; they think of themselves less
mc.why: Humility is not thinking poorly of yourself; true servants don't think less of themselves, they simply think of themselves less.

mc.stem: Why does the lesson call pride 'the root sin'?
options: It is the least common sin
It is the self-exaltation tangled into every other sin — the creature usurping God's throne
mc.why: Pride is closer to the root of all sin: the desire to be as God, to sit at the center where only God belongs; every other sin has that self-exaltation in it.

mc.stem: What 'false gods' did Charles Colson say we must repent of?
options: Materialism, power, success, and personal autonomy
mc.why: Colson said we must repent of idolatry — the false gods of materialism, power, success, and personal autonomy — each a way of making ourselves the center.

mc.stem: According to Philippians 2, what is the deepest reason to be humble?
options: Humility is the very mind of Christ, who made Himself of no reputation
mc.why: Humility is the mind of Christ: being in the form of God, He made Himself of no reputation, took the form of a servant, and humbled Himself to death on a cross.

mc.stem: What does it mean that humility is 'Christlikeness,' not a technique?
options: It is a personality trait some are born with
It is a skill mastered by practice alone
When we lower ourselves to serve and esteem others, we think the very thoughts of Jesus
mc.why: Humility is Christlikeness: lowering ourselves to serve and esteem others, we walk the downward path Jesus walked and let His mind be in us.

mc.stem: How does Colson say the world's standards compare to God's?
options: Every standard the world uses is the opposite of God's measure
mc.why: Every standard the world uses to judge men is the opposite of God's: the world prizes riches, recognition, and power; God exalts the poor in spirit, the humble, the servant.

mc.stem: In Matthew 20:25-28, how did Jesus redirect the desire for greatness?
options: Whoever desires to be great must become a servant
He said the strongest should rule
mc.why: Jesus did not abolish greatness but redirected it: it shall not be so among you; whoever would be great must be a servant, as He came to serve and give His life.

mc.stem: Whose feet did Jesus wash on the night He was betrayed, and what is striking about it?
options: No one's; He only taught about it
His disciples' feet, including Judas's, who would soon betray Him
mc.why: The Lord of glory took the slave's task and washed His disciples' feet — even Judas's — then said we ought to wash one another's feet. Real greatness kneels.

mc.stem: In the service Wayne attended, what did hammering the nail into the cross represent?
options: That Jesus was a victim of Rome alone
That we all had a hand in nailing Jesus to the cross — humility before God as sinners
mc.why: Each person drove the nail to confess that we all helped nail Jesus to the cross; the deepest humility is knowing we are sinners for whom Christ had to die.

mc.stem: What does the lesson say about borrowing leadership patterns from empire and corporation?
options: They are ideal for the church
They build religious hierarchies where men rule over men, contrary to Jesus
mc.why: Borrowing patterns from empire, military, and corporation builds hierarchies where men rule over men — pride in religious clothing, the very thing Jesus said should not be so.

mc.stem: How does Galatians 6:2 ('bear one another's burdens') connect to humility?
options: It takes humility to admit we have burdens and let others help us
mc.why: It takes humility to admit we have burdens; a proud heart hides its troubles to protect its image, but a humble heart is vulnerable and lets others help.

mc.stem: In the parable of the Pharisee and tax collector (Luke 18), who went home justified?
options: The tax collector who begged, 'God, be merciful to me a sinner'
The Pharisee who listed his virtues
mc.why: The broken, humble tax collector — not the impressive Pharisee — went home justified; God resists the one and gives grace to the other.

mc.stem: What promise is folded into 'humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God'?
options: That He may exalt us in due time
mc.why: We take the low place and trust God to do the lifting, in His time and way — 'that He may exalt you in due time.'

mc.stem: How is Christ Himself the pattern of humble-then-exalted?
options: He humbled Himself to death on a cross, therefore God highly exalted Him
mc.why: Christ humbled Himself to the death of the cross, and therefore God highly exalted Him and gave Him the name above every name — the descent was real, and so was the exaltation.

mc.stem: What does it mean to 'be clothed with humility'?
options: To wait until we feel humble
To deliberately put it on — choosing to think of ourselves less and serve, as Jesus wrapped a towel
mc.why: Humility is a garment we put on deliberately, as Jesus wrapped Himself in a towel; we don't wait to feel it but choose to serve and esteem others.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, how does humility actually free us?
options: It frees us from the exhausting work of defending and promoting ourselves, freeing us to love
mc.why: Humility frees us from the exhausting race for status and the work of defending and promoting ourselves, freeing us instead to love.

mc.stem: What is the final picture of humility the lesson leaves us with?
options: The God who left His throne, took a towel, and knelt — humility as following Him down
mc.why: Humility is the shape of a life that caught the mind of Christ — the God who left His throne, took a towel, and knelt; to be humble is to follow Him down.

fill.prompt: Peter writes, "God resists the ____, but gives grace to the humble" (1 Peter 5:5).

sa.prompt: Explain the 'divine economy' of 1 Peter 5:5-6 and why pride and humility matter so much to God.
sa.model: Peter says God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble, and then tells us to humble ourselves under God's mighty hand that He may exalt us in due time. This reveals an inverted economy in which the way up is down. Pride does not merely displease God; it sets a person against the very current of His grace, while humility opens the heart to receive it. So the whole Christian life runs on surrender rather than self-promotion: we lower ourselves and trust God to lift us in His own time and way. This is not a strategy for getting exalted, which would be pride wearing humility's clothes, but a genuine surrender that leaves the lifting to God.

sa.prompt: What is humility, and what is it NOT? Use the line about thinking of oneself less.
sa.model: Humility is easily misunderstood as self-hatred, groveling, or a low opinion of oneself, but that is not what Scripture means. As it has well been said, true servants do not think less of themselves; they simply think of themselves less. The proud person and the self-loathing person are alike in one way, for both are absorbed with themselves, and humility is the freedom of a self that has stopped staring at itself. Paul gives its positive shape: in lowliness of mind let each esteem others better than himself. Humility looks outward and upward, reckoning others worth genuine care and God worthy of all. It does not deny our gifts but remembers that whatever we have is a gift received, so the humble person takes a compliment or a correction with the same steadiness, since his sense of worth rests on neither.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson call pride 'the root sin,' and what false gods does Colson name?
sa.model: Pride is not just one sin among many but closer to the root of them all, for pride goes before destruction and a haughty spirit before a fall. It was pride that first turned a creature against the Creator, the desire to be as God and to sit at the center where only God belongs, and every other sin has some of that self-exaltation tangled into it. This is why God must resist the proud: pride is the human heart usurping God's throne, and His opposition to it is mercy, not cruelty. Charles Colson named its modern forms, saying we must repent of the false gods of materialism, power, success, and personal autonomy, each a way of making ourselves the center. Humility is simply the truth coming back into focus, that God is God and we are His creatures dependent on Him for every breath.

sa.prompt: Explain how Philippians 2:5-8 shows humility to be the mind of Christ.
sa.model: The deepest reason to be humble is that humility is the very mind of Christ. He who was God in His own right did not cling to His rights but made Himself of no reputation, took the form of a servant, and humbled Himself all the way down to the death of the cross. The whole movement of His life was downward, from heaven's throne to a manger, from glory to a cross, and every step of that descent was service. This means humility is not finally a technique or personality trait but Christlikeness. When we lower ourselves to serve, esteem others, and refuse to grasp at our rights, we are thinking the very thoughts of Jesus and walking the path He walked. The call to be humble is the call to let this mind be in us which was also in Christ Jesus, letting His self-giving love become our pattern.

sa.prompt: How does the gospel invert the world's ladder of values? Use Colson's contrasts.
sa.model: Once we see the mind of Christ, we realize how completely it overturns the world's scale of values. As Colson put it, every standard the world uses to judge men is the opposite of God's measure. The world says to be rich is to be blessed, but God blesses the poor in spirit. The world says to be recognized and applauded is to have arrived, but God exalts the humble. The world says to be powerful is to be great, but Jesus says you must become a servant to be great. This is not a minor adjustment to the world's ladder but a different ladder entirely, pointing the other direction, for the kingdom of God does not run on the same fuel as the kingdoms of men. This is freeing news, because the whole exhausting race for status is one we are free to step out of, since in Christ the lowest place has become the place of honor.

sa.prompt: Explain Matthew 20:25-28 and how the foot-washing of John 13 shows that 'real greatness kneels.'
sa.model: Jesus did not abolish the desire for greatness but redirected it, saying it shall not be so among you. Among the nations the rulers lord it over people, and greatness means having others under you, but in the kingdom greatness means getting under others to lift them, so whoever would be great must be a servant. He proves it by example, for the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve and to give His life a ransom for many. On the night He was betrayed, knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, Jesus rose, wrapped a towel around His waist, and washed His disciples' feet, including the feet of Judas who would betray Him within hours. The Lord of glory took the slave's task and said we ought to wash one another's feet. Here is the whole lesson in one picture: real greatness kneels.

sa.prompt: Describe the foot-washing-and-nail service and the two-fold meaning of humility it teaches.
sa.model: Wayne once attended a service where the pastor reenacted the closing days of Jesus' life. Everyone was asked to remove their shoes, and each person knelt and washed another's feet, showing that humility is something we do, not merely admire. Then at the front stood a wooden cross with a nail set in it, and every one of the worshipers took a turn driving that nail in, to confess that we had all helped nail Jesus to the cross. The service teaches a two-fold humility. First, foot-washing makes humility toward others personal and embodied, a thing done on the knees. Second, the nail roots humility before God, for the deepest humility is not merely thinking ourselves lower than other people but knowing we are sinners for whom Christ had to die, and that our own pride helped drive the nail.

sa.prompt: What does humility look like among God's people, in leadership and in honesty about struggles?
sa.model: Humility has sharp implications for the church. Too often we have borrowed leadership patterns from the empire, the military, and the corporate world, building religious hierarchies where men rule over men, the very thing Jesus said should not be so among us. Pride dressed in religious clothing produces domination, manipulation, and autocratic rule, ending in personal failure, while the early church knew leaders who walked in humility, were submitted to one another, served rather than dominated, and released others into ministry. Humility also shows in a quieter way, the willingness to be honest about our own struggles. Paul says to bear one another's burdens and so fulfill the law of Christ, and it takes humility even to admit we have burdens. A proud heart hides its troubles to protect its image, but a humble heart is vulnerable and forthright, and so receives the grace God gives through others.

sa.prompt: Use the Pharisee and tax collector (Luke 18) to explain the promise that God exalts the humble.
sa.model: Jesus pictured two men praying, a proud Pharisee who informed God of his virtues, and a tax collector who could only beat his breast and beg, God be merciful to me a sinner. It was the broken, humble man, not the impressive one, who went home justified, for God resists the one and gives grace to the other, and the way up really is down. There is a promise folded into the command to humble ourselves under God's mighty hand, namely that He may exalt us in due time. We are not asked to grovel in the dust forever but to take the low place and trust God to do the lifting, in His time and way. The pattern is Christ's own, who humbled Himself to the death of the cross, and therefore God highly exalted Him; what we surrender to God's mighty hand, that hand will one day raise.

sa.prompt: What does it mean to 'be clothed with humility,' and how does humility free us?
sa.model: Peter's command comes back with all its weight and hope: be clothed with humility. It is a garment we put on deliberately, the way Jesus deliberately wrapped Himself in a towel. We do not wait to feel humble but choose to think of ourselves less, to esteem others, to take the lower place, and to serve. As we do, we discover we are not diminished but freed, freed from the exhausting work of defending and promoting ourselves, and freed to love. Humility is therefore not one more virtue to achieve but the shape of a life that has caught the mind of Christ, the God who left His throne, took a towel, and knelt. To be humble is to follow Him down, confident that the God who raised Him will in due time raise all who walk that downward road with Him, for God resists the proud but to the humble gives grace upon grace.
